clue.text: Collector to demand payment, cornering mother behind street

indicators.note: to corner something is to hem it in, so the payment word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to dun is to press a debtor for payment

indicators.note: mother comes behind, i.e. after, street in the run of letters

parts.note: MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A debt collector chases payment, trapping somebody's mother at the back of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collector' suggests a debt collector, matching the surface, but it is a refuse collector.
explanation.definitionFit: A British bin man collects household rubbish, so he is a collector of refuse.

clue.text: Submissive party line adopted by French company

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: something adopted by another is taken in by it, so the line letter goes inside

parts.note: Cie is the French abbreviation for compagnie, company

explanation.surface: A meek political party line has been taken up by a French firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Docile means meekly obedient, readily giving way to others, which is being submissive.

clue.text: A shade wrong about English article being promoted

indicators.note: the wrong word goes about, i.e. around, the English letter

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoting a word raises it, so its letters read upwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shade of colour mistakenly placed around an English article that has moved up the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy brownish-yellow pigment, so it names a particular shade of colour.

clue.text: Do me a clear drink, with no hint of cabonation

parts.note: taken as written
to be clear about something is to be sure of it

indicators.note: the drink loses a letter, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a cup is a mixed drink such as a fruit or claret cup

indicators.note: a hint of a word is its first letter only

explanation.surface: A request: make me a clear drink without any fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabonation' is the setter's or printer's slip for carbonation; only its first letter C is used. 'Do' is a verb meaning be good enough, not the request it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To measure up is to be adequate or suffice, as in 'that will do'.

clue.text: One in love fix

indicators.note: one letter sits in the zero word, so it is placed inside

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, and nil is zero
A means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: Someone in love needs a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fasten or secure it in place, a sense of fix.

clue.text: Irishman backing foolish attack

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters of the two words are read in reverse

parts.note: dim means stupid or foolish
a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: An Irishman is supporting a stupid assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Diarmid is a traditional Irish and Gaelic male name, so it identifies a man from Ireland.

clue.text: The latest thing? Study that is taken on Catholic religious instruction is about right

indicators.note: the study takes on the following pieces, adding them after it
the whole preceding string is about, i.e. around, the right letter

parts.note: a den is a private study or workroom
ie, id est, means that is
RC stands for Roman Catholic
RI is the school abbreviation for religious instruction

explanation.surface: Learning that includes Catholic religious teaching has to do with what is right, as the newest fashion?
explanation.walkthrough: The R for 'right' goes in as the third letter, after DE.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'last cry', the phrase means the very newest fashion or development.

clue.text: Supplier of crossword blocking other newspaper feature is a pest

indicators.note: the setter's name blocks, i.e. sits in the way inside, the feature word

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a feature of a newspaper besides the crossword
Phi is the pseudonym of the setter of this crossword

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler's piece crowding out the paper's other features is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi, the setter, puts himself into the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly suck sap from plants, so gardeners treat them as an insect pest.

clue.text: Man mostly against love, not quite a hero comedy role

indicators.note: mostly means not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: male means a man
v, versus, means against
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a lion is a brave or celebrated person, a hero

explanation.surface: A man who mostly opposes love, falling short of heroism, plays a comic part.
explanation.walkthrough: MALVOLIO is the puritanical steward in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, who is famously hostile to merriment.
explanation.definitionFit: The steward gulled by forged letters in Twelfth Night is a classic part in a Shakespeare comedy.

clue.text: Queue for Charon's ferry? A time that shouldn't be missed

definitions.meaning: Charon ferries the souls of the departed across the Styx, so those waiting form a queue of the deceased

definitions.text: A time that shouldn't be missed
definitions.meaning: a fixed time limit by which work must be finished

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the last date for finishing a task and, read literally, a queue of the departed.

clue.text: Church woman's story beginning to ruin French nobleman

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name
a story can be a lie, a fib

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A churchwoman's tale begins the downfall of a French aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a French knight, the lowest title of the old French nobility.

clue.text: Woman concealed article about introduction to lover

indicators.note: the concealing word and article go about, i.e. around, the next letter

parts.note: hid means concealed

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman has hidden something concerning the start of an affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilda is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Cheek to accept new German team

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: lip is insolent talk, cheek
neu is the German word for new

explanation.surface: Having the nerve to take on a brand-new German side.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-up is the list of players chosen for a match, the side fielded.

clue.text: Wolf could do for them?

parts.note: a wolf could kill ducks and geese; also the letters of the word wolf are a wild arrangement of the birds' second half

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: a wolf could 'do for' (kill) these birds, and WOLF is a wild rearrangement of FOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild ducks and geese are game birds a predatory wolf could catch and kill.

clue.text: Given accommodation with no end of space? Always a time when payment's due

indicators.note: the accommodation word goes without one letter, which is removed

parts.note: soldiers are quartered when given lodging

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: ay or aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Lodged without any spare room, there is always a date when rent falls due.
explanation.walkthrough: It is the second E of the lodging word, the end of 'space', that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarter days are the four days of the year on which rents and other payments traditionally fall due in England.

clue.text: Front of Regency building about certain (almost) for revival

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
the building word goes about, i.e. around, the trimmed piece

parts.note: an erection is a building

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is cut

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: The facade of a Regency building is being restored, almost for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising again from death or disuse is a revival, as of a fashion or a person.

clue.text: Patrons start to congregate right above box

indicators.note: in a down clue the right piece is placed above the box piece
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
tele and box are both informal words for a television set

explanation.surface: Customers begin to gather right over a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's clientele is its body of customers or patrons.

clue.text: One engaged in cruel words as sufficing for fashionable hits

indicators.note: the one letter is engaged, i.e. held, inside the words
one word suffices for, i.e. stands in place of, the other

parts.note: insults are cruel or offensive remarks
in means fashionable
taken as written
A means one

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a cruel exchange, as if that justified stylish blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like a description of the hits, but it names the letters that 'as' replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaults are physical attacks, and hits are blows that strike someone.

clue.text: GP's first to extol endless sleep for eye condition

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter
endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: to laud is to praise highly, to extol
a coma is a deep unconscious sleep

explanation.surface: A GP begins praising endless rest as a cure for an eye complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaucoma is raised pressure within the eye that damages the optic nerve, an eye disease.

clue.text: Start with profile, scrawled? It's often full-frontal instead

indicators.note: scrawled writing is jumbled and untidy, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Begin by sketching a side view roughly, though a portrait usually faces forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange START and PROFILE together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist painting their own image in a mirror usually shows the face head-on rather than from the side.

clue.text: Player's one great shot, mostly crazy

parts.note: a man is a player in a team or game
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable serve, a great shot in tennis

explanation.surface: A player's single great shot is mostly crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Maniac can be used as an adjective meaning wildly mad or frenzied.

clue.text: German writer suppressing origin of the German style

parts.note: Thomas Mann was a German novelist

indicators.note: suppressing the origin of a word removes its first letter

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A German novelist holds back the start of the German way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner is a way of doing something, a style.

clue.text: Explorer, please note, taking in US state

indicators.note: the please word takes in, i.e. surrounds, the state abbreviation

parts.note: to amuse is to please or entertain
ND is the abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: An explorer asks for attention, absorbing an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Amundsen was the Norwegian polar explorer who first reached the South Pole.

clue.text: Live debate's beginning satisfactorily

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: well means satisfactorily

explanation.surface: A live debate is getting off to a good start.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live in a place, to reside.

clue.text: Gossip about King and Queen seen around a European capital

indicators.note: the gossip word goes about, i.e. around, the royal pair

parts.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes and gossip about someone

indicators.note: the royal letters are seen around, i.e. either side of, the a

parts.note: R is from Regina, queen

explanation.surface: Talk of a king and queen being spotted around a European capital.
explanation.walkthrough: ANKARA, Turkey's capital, lies in Asia Minor, so calling it European is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey, a country partly in Europe.

clue.text: Responsibility of a rising star?

parts.note: o' is a short form of of, as in o'clock

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the Sun is a star

explanation.surface: The duties of an up-and-coming celebrity?
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty that falls on someone, a responsibility.

clue.text: John's energy is uncontrolled

parts.note: john is American slang for a lavatory, a loo; its plural gives loos
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A man called John has energy that runs wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John's' reads as a man's possessive but is the plural of john, a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loose is not held or restrained, free of control.

clue.text: Contributors to food-store discussing salad plant

indicators.note: the contributing word is added to, inside, the shop word

parts.note: a deli, delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared food
and is the word that adds or contributes one item to another
on means about or discussing

explanation.surface: Suppliers to a grocery talk about a leafy salad ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contributors' stands for the conjunction that adds one thing to another; 'to' places it in the shop word.
explanation.definitionFit: Young dandelion leaves are eaten raw in salads, so it is a salad plant as well as a weed.

clue.text: Artist sent screenplay for broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter sent in a script to be aired on radio or television.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Spencer was an English painter known for scenes set in the village of Cookham.
explanation.definitionFit: The English painter of The Resurrection, Cookham was an artist of the twentieth century.
